title: Hackers reportedly breached US Air Force Cloud One platform, Reuters says
date_note: The page gives no earlier day than its 27 November publication; it says the intrusion surfaced during the past month.
geo_basis: country (the US Air Force; no city stated)
summary: The Next Web, relaying Reuters, reports that hackers broke into Cloud One, the US Air Force's main cloud computing platform, according to three people familiar with the matter. Reuters says the intrusion surfaced during a system upgrade and it could not establish who was responsible or whether data was stolen. The Air Force told Reuters it does not comment on the security posture of specific networks and systems.
plain: Reuters, relayed by The Next Web, reports that hackers got into the US Air Force's main cloud computing platform, Cloud One. Reuters could not establish who was behind it or whether data was stolen.
exec: Reuters' sources say the US Air Force's main cloud platform was breached; the cause and any data loss are unknown, and the Air Force has not commented on specifics.

validation.note: Only The Next Web (relaying Reuters, three unnamed sources) was read; the Reuters page, Cybernews and CNA could not be loaded (403 or blocked); no Air Force statement beyond a refusal to comment was read.
